description.short_caption: Radiograph of the left wrist showing lytic lesions in the distal radius.
description.detailed_description: This radiograph depicts the left wrist, including the distal radius, ulna, and carpal bones. There are prominent lytic lesions visible in the distal radius, characterized by areas of bone destruction with irregular margins. The surrounding bone appears intact, and no obvious periosteal reaction is noted. The carpal bones and ulna appear unaffected.

Case_16003/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and extremities.

description.short_caption: CT scan showing abnormalities in the abdomen and pelvis, including soft tissue and bony structures.
description.detailed_description: This CT image includes coronal and axial views of the abdomen and pelvis. The coronal view shows the lumbar spine, kidneys, and surrounding soft tissues. The axial inset highlights the pelvic region, including the hip joint and adjacent structures. There appear to be abnormalities in the soft tissue and bony structures, potentially indicative of infection or inflammation. No contrast enhancement is evident in this image.
visible_findings: lumbar spine visible in coronal view
soft tissue abnormalities in the pelvic region
hip joint visible in axial inset

Case_16003/figure5.jpg.source_caption: CT and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lumbar spine.

description.short_caption: CT and MRI of the lumbar spine showing vertebral abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a sagittal CT scan (left) and a sagittal T2-weighted MRI (right) of the lumbar spine. The CT scan highlights bony structures, showing vertebral bodies and intervertebral disc spaces. The MRI provides soft tissue contrast, revealing intervertebral discs and potential abnormalities in the spinal canal. There appears to be evidence of vertebral endplate irregularities and possible disc space narrowing, suggesting degenerative or infectious changes.
visible_findings: sagittal CT of lumbar spine showing vertebral bodies and disc spaces
sagittal T2-weighted MRI of lumbar spine with soft tissue contrast

Case_16003/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Physical finding on the left posterior thigh.

description.short_caption: Ulcerated lesion with erythematous and violaceous borders on the left posterior thigh.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows an oval-shaped ulcerated lesion on the skin of the left posterior thigh. The lesion has a central area of necrosis or granulation tissue, surrounded by erythematous and violaceous borders. The surrounding skin appears slightly indurated, and there is no visible purulent discharge. The lesion is well-demarcated and suggests an inflammatory or infectious process.

Case_16003/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Pathological examination of the gluteal aspirate (H and E stain).

description.short_caption: Histopathology of gluteal aspirate showing fungal elements (H&E stain).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a gluteal aspirate stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The main panel reveals numerous inflammatory cells, including neutrophils, and scattered fungal elements. The inset highlights round fungal structures with thick walls and occasional budding, consistent with yeast forms. The background shows necrotic debris and cellular infiltrates, indicative of an infectious process.
visible_findings: round fungal elements with thick walls

description.short_caption: Circular, erythematous, scaly skin lesion with central clearing.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a circular skin lesion with a well-demarcated, erythematous border and central clearing. The lesion appears scaly, with some areas of hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation. The surrounding skin is unremarkable. The findings are consistent with a dermatologic condition, possibly fungal in origin, such as tinea corporis.

Case_16003/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Pathological examination of the gluteal aspirate (GMS stain).

description.short_caption: GMS stain of gluteal aspirate showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a GMS (Gomori methenamine silver) stain of a gluteal aspirate. The field contains round to oval fungal elements with thick, darkly stained walls, consistent with yeast forms. Some of the yeast cells appear to have budding, indicative of replication. The background tissue is lightly stained, providing contrast to the fungal structures. The image includes magnified insets for clearer visualization of the fungal morphology.
